text:
sam: heads-up — after the kernel hint flip on mistral-7b-gqa in prod-1 we’re seeing a ~12% p95 latency regression and a 9% drop in tokens/sec for steady-state batching.
anya: ugh. which hint exactly? the fused-attn -> tiled-attn swap? :grimacing:
dave: correct — we switched to tiled-attn (kernel v2.4) to address memory spikes but perf slipped.
sam: repro on staging: single-socket a100, batcher config B07, seq=512. baseline tiled-attn off: 130 tok/s. tiled-attn on: 118 tok/s. p95 from 42ms -> 47ms.
perf-bot: perf-run summary attached: run_id=run-2026-03-17-19, p50/p95/p99/timeouts. KV cache hit rate steady ~81%.
kai: can you paste the profiler flame snippet? I want to see kernel time vs memcpy vs batching overhead.
sam: sure — trimmed flame (most noisy parts):
```
- tiled_attn_kernel 38%
- kv_slot_lookup 12%
- batch_coalesce 9%
- cudaMemcpyAsync 7%
- other_kernels 34%
```
jess: tiled_attn taking 38% is surprising — on earlier runs it was ~24% for same seq distribution. maybe head packing changed? any change in num_key_value_heads or kv_dim mapping?
dave: we did switch to GQA mapping for that model variant (num_key_value_heads=8 -> 16) to increase parallelism for larger batches.
anya: ah that could explain it — tiled-attn's tiling scheme expects head_stride aligned to 16 in the kernel; when heads doubled, memory layout changed and kernels launched different tile sizes.
perf-bot: microbench: tiled_attn kernel latency doubles when head_stride % 16 != 0 for seq>256 on this kernel version.
sam: confirmed: kv layout now has head_stride 12 for the way our packer arranges kv for MQA->GQA conversion — so misaligned.
kai: options:
- revert hint to fused-attn temporarily (fast rollback)
- adjust packer to force head_stride alignment (padding) — costs memory but might fix kernel perf
- tweak tiled-attn kernel to handle unaligned strides (longer term)
- change batcher heuristic to avoid sequences that trigger pathological tiling
dave: quick experiment — I padded KV stride to 16 on staging and re-ran: tok/s went up to 127, p95 down to 43ms. hit rate unchanged.
anya: nice. what's the memory overhead? any OOM risk for peak seqs?
dave: ~3% memory increase on typical load, worst-case ~8% for seq=1024 (still under limit on prod-1). I think safe for a rollout behind opt-in.
jess: we should also check paged KV fragmentation — padding could increase paging in the paged-kv layout and worsen fragmentation.
sam: I profiled paged allocations: fragmentation metric before=0.12, after padding=0.18 for the tested run. so fragmentation rose.
kai: tradeoff: small perf regain vs fragmentation that can cause long-tail spikes on high concurrency. we need an A/B.
anya: propose: A) revert kernel hint in prod-1 immediately to stop regression (hotfix), B) run A/B on prod-2 with padded stride + tiled-attn to measure tail and fragmentation under real traffic, C) longer-term: update kernel to be stride-agnostic or update packer to pack differently per kernel.
dave: +1. I can push rollback today. who will manage A/B on prod-2 and the observation dashboards?
sam: I’ll own the dashboards (latency, tok/s, kv-frag, gpu-mem, p95 tails). kai can set the A/B rollout config and traffic split.
kai: can do. will route 10% to variant-b (padded stride + tiled-attn). infra-bot: scheduling canary rollout for infra-prod-2, split=10/90, change_id=ch-8342.
infra-bot: canary scheduled: start=2026-03-18T02:10Z, duration=2h, rollback_on=latency>5% or errors>1%.
perf-bot: added evaluation suite: microbench per kernel, kv-frag checks, batching histograms, and the prompt-set regen to ensure quality unchanged.
jess: also run a kernel-level microbench for unaligned head_strides on Qwen variants — we may hit similar behavior elsewhere.
anya: note: RoPE scaling changes last month may have increased average seqs because we kept more context in cache — affects batching distribution. worth correlating.
sam: good point — linking to session: recent retention tweak led to 14% more cached prefixes for chat flows which increases long-seq tail.
kai: for the immediate roll back, dave — add a short blurb in deploy notes about causing tiled-attn discovery and link this thread.
dave: on it. I'll revert the hint in the next deploy window and attach the perf diff.
sam: after rollback, we’ll run the A/B and get concrete numbers. If padding is safe, we can add dynamic packer path: if kernel==tiled-attn and heads unaligned -> pad; else leave.
ya: we should also add a kernel selection rule to the smart router: prefer fused-attn for models with head_stride unaligned to 16 until kernels are fixed.
jess: creating a follow-up task in eng-runtime backlog: kernel_stride-robustness + packer-padding + router-rule. I’ll link PRs.
perf-bot: next steps checklist added to ticket: TKT-4891. items: rollback, canary, microbench, kernel fix proposal.
sam: thanks everyone. let's monitor after rollback and sync tomorrow 10:30am PT for results. :thumbsup:
